case_title: Bhaskarrao & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour/acquaintance; alleged prior quarrel over Rs.50 with Accused No. 4 (alleged, not proved). PW1 said their relationship was cordial.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.147, s.148, s.452 r/w s.149, s.302 r/w s.149, s.506; SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act s.3(i)(x) (as charged/alleged)
weapon: Sticks, axe, sword and iron pipe
evidence_type: Eyewitness (related witnesses), circumstantial, medical (post-mortem), recovery of weapons and clothing, motive
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted all accused tried (accused 1 to 15) of all charges; no sentence
high_court_outcome: Reversed acquittal and convicted all appellants except accused 6 (dead). Sentences: 2 years for ss.147, 148, 452; life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine each for s.302 r/w 149; 6 months and Rs.500 fine for s.506 (sentences concurrent)
neutral_facts: On the evening of 19 June 1995, an altercation reportedly took place between the victim and one of the accused over a sum of money, near a grocery shop in the village; the victim was said to have slapped that accused during the scuffle. Later that evening, a group of about sixteen persons, armed with sticks, a sword, an axe and an iron pipe, allegedly entered the victim's house, dragged him out, and assaulted his hands and legs. The assault allegedly continued while he was dragged along the road and to a field, where his right palm was reportedly cut off. The victim's wife, who witnessed part of the incident, reportedly hid in a cattle shed for about two hours before informing a neighbour, and a complaint was lodged the following day. The victim's body was found in a field on 21 June 1995 without the right palm, which was found at some distance. Several witnesses, most of them related to the victim or to one another, gave statements about the number of assailants, the lighting, and the sequence of events, and their accounts differed on several points. The witness who recorded the complaint said the earlier quarrel was not mentioned in it. A panch witness for seizure of clothing did not support the prosecution, and weapons recovered at the instance of the accused were found to have no bloodstains on chemical analysis. The post-mortem doctor opined that death resulted from heavy blood loss due to amputation of the hand, with no injury to vital organs. No test identification parade was held.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from blood loss due to amputation of the right hand/palm; incised wounds to wrist, forearm and leg; no injury to vital organs
number_of_offences: 6 charged (IPC ss.147, 148, 452 r/w 149, 302 r/w 149, 506; SC/ST Act s.3(i)(x)); 0 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Not found; the Court held an intention to kill and unlawful assembly were not established
motive: alleged: earlier quarrel over Rs.50 in which the deceased slapped Accused No. 4 (not proved); alleged caste-based motive also not proved
key_evidence_accepted: Court relied on the post-mortem opinion that death was from blood loss due to amputation, the chemical report showing no bloodstains on recovered weapons, and the contradictions in the evidence. No eyewitness account was accepted as proving the amputation or the identity of assailants.
witness_credibility: Witnesses were related and their evidence was scrutinised with caution. PW1 showed many improvements and FIR omissions, and her account of the quarrel was hearsay. PWs 2, 3 and 5 contradicted each other on the number of accused. PW4 made improvements. PW11 and PW13 (panch) did not support the prosecution, PW6 could not identify his signatures, and PW7's medical evidence did not corroborate the case.
custody_duration: About three years before enlargement on bail (as noted by the Court)
bail_history: Accused were enlarged on bail at some stage (date not stated); bail bonds discharged by Supreme Court order
trial_duration: offence: 19 June 1995; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 21 December 2013; Supreme Court: 26 April 2018
legal_representation: Accused: V.V.S. Rao, Sr. Adv. (for Accused No. 8); Ms. Anagha S. Desai (for Accused Nos. 2, 7, 9, 10 to 14); Dharmendra Kumar Sinha (for Accused Nos. 1, 3, 4, 5); also Varun Mathur, Tadimalla Baskar Gowtham, Subodh K. Pathan and Nishant Ramakantrao Katneshwarkar listed for the parties. State: Mr. Nishant Ramakantrao Katneshwarkar
investigation_status: FIR/complaint registered (Crime No. 72 of 1995, 20 June 1995); investigation completed; charges framed against accused 1 to 15; trial held
procedural_irregularity: No test identification parade was held; the Court treated this as fatal to the prosecution case
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted all accused (1 to 15). High Court: reversed acquittal and convicted all except accused 6 (dead). Supreme Court: appeals allowed, High Court order set aside, trial court acquittal restored.
prosecution_argument: Minor discrepancies were given undue importance; the accused in pursuance of a common object dragged the deceased and assaulted him with sticks, axe and sword; PW1 tried to save him; the High Court correctly assessed the evidence.
defence_argument: Story concocted; no eyewitness to the murder; no bloodstains on weapons; interested inter-related witnesses; quarrel introduced later; no test identification parade; no motive; medical evidence did not corroborate; High Court wrongly interfered with acquittal.
legal_principle_applied: Appellate court must be very cautious in overturning acquittal and may do so only for compelling reasons and substantial grounds; circumstantial evidence must form an unbroken chain; interested witnesses' evidence must be scrutinised; motive has a role but its absence alone cannot dislodge the case.
precedent_relied_upon: Surajpal Singh 1952 CriLJ 331; Dalip Singh [1954] 1 SCR 145; Masalti [1964] 8 SCR 133; Darya Singh [1964] 3 SCR 397; Harbans Kaur 2005 CriLJ 2199; Namdeo (2007) 14 SCC 150; Hari Shanker (1996) 9 SCC 40; Ujjagar Singh (2007) 13 SCC 90; Kishanpal (2008) 16 SCC 73; Bipin Kumar Mondal (2010) 12 SCC 91; Tahsildar Singh AIR 1959 SC 1012; Tota Singh 1987 CriLJ 974; Ramesh Babulal Doshi 1996 CriLJ 2867
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds of the appellants discharged; pending applications disposed of
